location: line 292, def:existence:truecontext, clause (iii) 'that bridge is sound: whenever $c$ establishes $\varphi$ and $\sigma$ holds in the actual world, so does $\varepsilon$'
problem: Given Gamma, the canonical state of c and the actual world are fixed, so 'whenever' ranges over one case. Under (i) and (ii), clause (iii) is then equivalent to 'epsilon is actually true', and 'true enough' collapses to 'phi derivable in c, some bridge to epsilon exists, and epsilon is true'. That loses the world-relative bridge soundness the next paragraph says must be certified. The round-2 re-verification flagged the clause as degenerate, and it was never repaired in T6 or in the paper.
proposed_fix: Replace (iii) with: "(iii) that bridge is \emph{sound} in the sense of \Cref{def:physics:calculus}: every instance of it preserves truth at every world $w\in W_\rho$ admitted by the background, i.e.\ whenever $c$ establishes $\varphi$ and $\sigma$ holds at $w$, $\varepsilon$ holds at $w$ (quantifying only over the actual world would make (iii) equivalent to the truth of $\varepsilon$)."

location: line 190 ('Scope': 'For any single finite agenda the finitely many rational inequalities defining $\Pi_F$ ... give finitely many counting sequents that characterize coherence')
problem: Pi_F always lies in the affine subspace P(phi)+P(phi*)=1. Turning its defining (in)equalities into counting sequents uses negation coherence: counting sequents alone cannot impose P(phi)+P(phi*) <= 1, since P identically 1 satisfies every valid counting sequent (thm:existence:definetti). The round-2 re-verification flagged the sentence as too broad, and the hypothesis is still missing.
proposed_fix: Replace with: 'For any single finite agenda (a union of complementary pairs) and negation-coherent $P$, the finitely many rational facet inequalities of $\Pi_F$ give finitely many counting sequents that characterize coherence (\Cref{thm:existence:definetti}); what \Cref{thm:existence:arity,thm:existence:threshold} rule out ...' (rest unchanged).
